newsitem.title: CHINA: China state listings would curb speculation - official.
newsitem.headline: China state listings would curb speculation - official.

text.p: China needs to increase the size of the float of listed state-owned companies in order to reduce speculation on the nation's stock markets, an official for managing state assets said on Monday.

More shares held by the state directly and through state institutions with so called "legal person shares" should be made available to public shareholders to make it harder to manipulate the market, said Zhang Jixiang, an official of the National Administration of State Property.
"If legal person and state shares are not made liquid it will restrict the market," said Zhang, who is director of the Administration's Assets Appraisal Administration Centre.
"In many cases, most of the shares are off the market. This leads to speculation" of the listed shares, he told a conference on reorganising state assets.
Many state companies have listed only a small portion of their shares, keeping the remainder in the hands of state enterprises or state institutions.

This was designed to ensure continued state control over these companies after listing. But China is trying to raise capital for many ailing state companies, and many economic policy makers are looking to list more companies in areas that are not considered vital to the government.
China's securities regulators are also eager to reduce speculation which has led to high volatility on the nation's two stock markets in Shanghai and the southern city of Shenzhen.
Zhang also said that many companies planning to issue shares had only a vague idea of what they would do with the money after their public offering.
"Many of these companies are just hoping to list to take advantage of a strong stock market," he said. "But they do not have a plan of how to use the capital they raise to compete better."
He added that many companies were not adequately prepared for future payments of dividends, and as a result investors had a low return on their investments.
